entities.summary: Herod Antipas, was a 1st-century Herodian ruler of Galilee and Perea, in the time of the Herodian Tetrarchy. He bore the title of tetrarch and is referred to as both "Herod the Tetrarch" and "King Herod" in the New Testament. He was a son of Herod the Great and a grandson of Antipater the Idumaean. Known for his role in the executions of John the Baptist and Jesus of Nazareth, his name is often associated with tyranny and persecution. Herod Antipas was a monarchs & rulers from Judea (b. 19 BCE, Judea). Recognized as a landmark figure with global significance (referenced in 0 Wikipedia editions). Relevant to political systems and imperial and colonial studies.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Herod Antipas's reign marked a pivotal moment in Christian history, as his execution of John the Baptist and Jesus of Nazareth had far-reaching consequences for early Christianity. His actions are referenced in all four canonical Gospels and have been studied by scholars for centuries.
